questions.enonce_markdown:
'The fear of Judgement Day and the joy or torment that will follow remains a fundamental guiding principle in Islam'. Assess the validity of this statement.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Belief in the Last Day (*al-Akhira*) is one of the six articles of faith in Islam. To 'assess the validity' of the statement is to examine how far the thought of Judgement, Paradise and Hell guides Muslim belief and conduct, and to consider other principles that also guide it.

**1. Belief in the Last Day.** Muslims believe that the world will end, that all people will be raised, and that each will be judged on the Day of Resurrection (*Yawm al-Qiyama*). The Qur'an speaks of the record of deeds, of the weighing of actions, and of the final reward in Paradise (*Jannah*) or punishment in Hell (*Jahannam*). The early surahs of Makkah warn strongly of this Day.

**2. Evidence that it is a guiding principle.**
(i) *Accountability.* Believers know that they will answer for all their deeds, so they try to be honest, just and kind.
(ii) *Worship.* Prayer, fasting, almsgiving and pilgrimage are done in the hope of reward and the fear of failing before God.
(iii) *Social justice.* The Qur'an links the Last Day with care for orphans, the poor and the weak, and condemns oppression and cheating.
(iv) *God-consciousness (taqwa).* Fear of God and awareness of the Day of Judgement are a basis of the moral life.
(v) *Patience in trial.* The hope of Paradise helps Muslims bear suffering.

**3. Balance of fear and hope.** Islam does not teach fear alone. Muslims stress that God is the Most Merciful and Forgiving; nearly every surah of the Qur'an begins by invoking God as the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Fear (*khawf*) is balanced by hope (*raja'*). Some Sufi writers stressed love of God above fear of Hell or desire for Paradise.

**4. Other guiding principles.** The statement should not be taken to mean that this is the only principle. Equally basic are the oneness of God (*tawhid*), the authority of the Qur'an and of the Prophet's example, the five pillars, justice, and mercy towards creation.

**5. Evaluation.** The statement is valid in that belief in the Last Day is fundamental and gives moral seriousness to a Muslim's life. It would be less accurate if it suggested that fear alone motivates Muslims, since love, gratitude and hope are equally emphasised.

**Conclusion.** The Day of Judgement is one of the most important guiding principles in Islam, but it works together with God's mercy and other basic beliefs.
